parameters.name: region
parameters.description: price_demand region label the window is averaged over, e.g. VIC1 or NSW1

parameters.name: metric_column
parameters.description: numeric price_demand column to average, e.g. rrp or total_demand_mw

parameters.name: start_ts
parameters.description: window start as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, the exclusive lower bound on settlement_ts

parameters.name: end_ts
parameters.description: window end as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, the inclusive upper bound on settlement_ts

sql_template: SELECT avg({metric_column}) FROM price_demand WHERE region = '{region}' AND settlement_ts > CAST('{start_ts}' AS TIMESTAMP) AND settlement_ts <= CAST('{end_ts}' AS TIMESTAMP)

steps.cmd: fill every slot of sql_template from the question's declared parameters and save it as filled.sql
steps.pass: filled.sql contains no remaining {slot}, quotes no value of its own, and names only columns of price_demand
the JSON prints one row with the single averaged column and carries no error key
PASS question, PASS sql, PASS values

notes: settlement_ts is the END of the 5-minute interval, so the window needs > start and <= end: a >= start AND < end filter drops the interval that ends exactly on the upper bound and admits one that ends exactly on the lower one.
average the raw column and round nowhere in the SQL - rounding each interval before averaging changes the figure, and the answer is compared against the unrounded aggregate.
region and metric_column come from the question's own declared parameters, so the window shape never changes between siblings of this family.
